items.title: Dave Frishberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001
items.q: Carmen McRae and people like that, they bend it around.

ctx.x: Dorough on the other hand is a different kind of composer. He’s not bound by his own limitations. Dorough writes for a voice, and he’s a more thorough composer, a more versatile composer than I am. He writes a lot of songs that singers get their teeth into. “Love Came on Stealthy Fingers” and songs like that are ballads in demand by singers, and they use it to show off their voice. Carmen McRae and people like that, they bend it around. I don’t have a lot of songs like that.
Yeah. If you look back in your career — this is kind of a hard question — but are any gigs or certain times that stand out as really memorable, either negative or positive or humorous reasons?
